text:
maya: Heads up — seeing blockmap/metadata corruption on /dev/nvme0n1 of gnode-114 after the nightly batch. GPU pods can't provision, kube shows FailedMount + IO errors. Anyone oncall?

liam: ugh. Can you paste the dmesg and `smartctl -a`?

maya: short logs pasted below, full logs in GCS: gs://redwood-logs/gnode-114/2123456789.log

maya: ```
[  123.456789] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 204800
[  123.456792] EXT4-fs error (device nvme0n1p1): ext4_journal_start_sb: Detected aborted journal
[  123.456795] metadata checksum mismatch on block 1024
smartctl 7.2 2020-12-30: Device doesn't support SMART
```

jordan: that metadata checksum line looks like filesystem-level corruption — probably from an unclean shutdown or drive firmware flake during heavy write burst. Nightly batch writes are big (model checkpoints), right?

maya: yes, checkpoint + shuffle write pattern. We saw sustained ~200k iops during the window.

alice: any chance it's the ephemeral-cleaner kicking off while the batch is writing? we tuned cleaner to agressive last month to reduce cost.

liam: good call — cleaner + heavy write could step on GC. If the drive firmware has weak atomicity, concurrent trim/erase could corrupt metadata.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3245 (auto). PagerDuty notified (oncall: jordan).

jordan: I'm on it. I'll cordon gnode-114 and start a controlled drain. If other nodes show similar dmesg pattern we should pause the nightly and stop scheduling new GPU jobs.

maya: cordoned. Two other nodes (gnode-117, gnode-119) show increased re-try rates in iostat but not full corruption yet.

liam: Plan proposal: 1) pause nightly job queue, 2) cordon+drain affected nodes, 3) snapshot logs + attempt read-only fsck, 4) if fsck can't recover, reprovision instance with fresh ephemeral and reprovision the GPU pods, 5) roll back cleaner aggressiveness and add a transient scheduling lock during bulk writes. Thoughts?

alice: add: increase ephemeral-cleaner backoff to avoid overlap window, and add KV-cache to reduce checkpoint churn. Also tag these batches to land on nodes with newer firmware if available.

jordan: agreed. Doing step 1 now (paused queues). Starting read-only fsck on gnode-114 to see if mountable. If not, we'll reprovision — estimate 30-45m to reprovision and requeue jobs.

sre-engineer: FYI cost note: reprovision + re-run nightly will burn ~8 GPU-hours (~$120) if we reprovision 3 nodes. Also if we pause too long customers may see latency, but uptime is lower risk than corrupt data.

liam: also raising a ticket with the vendor — sequence looks like a firmware corner-case under high sustained write+trim. If vendor confirms, we may need fleet-wide firmware push or node-level scheduling constraints.

maya: thanks. I'll add the logs and the iostat heatmaps to INC-2026-3245. tagging @jordan for updates. :white_check_mark:

jordan: update: fsck returned unrecoverable metadata errors. Proceeding with reprovision. I'll patch the reprovision script to ensure ephemeral-cleaner is disabled on first boot for 2 hours and to prefer drives with firmware >= 3.1.

alice: after reprovision we should run a soak with synthetic checkpoint writes to validate before reintroducing production batches.

jordan: agreed. I'll run soak and then unpause queue once soak is green. ETA 2.5h.

ops-bot: INC-2026-3245 updated by jordan: nodes reprovisioned, soak started.

liam: follow-up action item: schedule a rolling firmware validation across a small subset of fleet next week, and revert cleaner to conservative defaults until we confirm safety. I'll file a RFC.

maya: thanks team. tagging this thread to the postmortems channel after incident closes.

alice: small note for product: consider shifting heavy checkpointing to object storage rather than local ephemeral for bursty jobs — reduces IOPS pressure.

jordan: closing loop here — I reintroduced jobs after a 45m soak, all green. Will keep monitoring latency and error rates for next 24h.

maya: great. please keep incremental updates in INC-2026-3245 and the postmortem with timeline. :pray:
